built.notes:
File: design/flow/screens/home-a.html. I did not touch game-classic.html.

I followed the user's wording: the sheet is labelled 'NEW BOARDING PASS', which matches the reference band. The list is a departures list on boarding-pass paper, not a split-flap board.

The screen is built from data: the areas and their decks live in one array at the top of the script. The chips are generated from that array and sit in a strip that scrolls sideways, edge to edge, so eight areas will fit. If there are many decks, the list scrolls inside the pass and the page itself never scrolls.

Accessibility and safe zones:
- Chips are 40px tall but have a 48px tap area, and they use aria-pressed (selected state is shown by an ink fill, not by colour alone).
- Rows and destinations are full-width buttons with aria-labels.
- The sheet is an aria-modal dialog. It closes with Esc, a tap on the scrim, or the X button, and focus goes back to the deck row that opened it.
- Reduced motion is respected. The top 50px and bottom 30px are kept free.

Only the CLF row has data-demo.

screens.summary: Wallet home: the four decks are boarding passes stacked like a wallet. The front pass shows the amber carrier band, a large deck code, the deck name, an Area / Cards / Best streak field grid, a 'Seen' flight path with the plane at the progress point, and a full-width 'Choose route' button in the stub. The passes behind show only their paper top with a small amber platform tile, platform, deck name and code. Tapping one swaps it with the front pass using a spring FLIP motion. Signature detail: the destination leg is drawn as three blank dashes labelled 'Section and mode next', so 'Choose route' reads as filling in the other half of the ticket.
screens.openQuestions: 1) RND best streak is shown as 5. The brief only gave 12% seen, and showing no streak on a played deck would look like a bug. 2) The filter has an 'All' chip (selected by default) in front of the area chips. 3) Swapping is a straight trade: the old front pass takes the tapped pass's place in the stack, so it does not move to the back. 4) Platform is the 'carrier' in the band (AWS, Google Cloud, Next.js) and area sets the glyph (cloud for Cloud, </> for Frontend). The Frontend glyph is new. 5) Should the app remember which pass was in front last time? CLF is assumed here.
screens.shotCheck: Four rounds. built.notes:
I've made the four screens in the boarding pass style you asked for, and all four pass the screenshot check. They're in design/flow/screens: mode-select.html, game-streak.html, game-lives.html and game-timed.html. The screenshots are in design/flow/shots as <id>-1.png and <id>-2.png.

- **game-classic.html was not changed.** No new colours or tokens were added; the :root block is copied as is.
- **Changes beyond the header and Class field.** A Card field like '04 / 10' makes no sense without a fixed length, so in the three game screens the Card field, the stub row label and the barcode data now use the mode name and a plain card number. Swipe, data-state, data-result and data-answer work as in the reference.
- **Next card.** Streak and Three lives keep the Next card button. In Streak it changes to 'See results' after a wrong answer. Timed has no Next card button because the brief removes the explanation step.
- **Timed stamp timing.** The stamp is held about 1 s from the tap, not 700 ms. The screenshot tool captures 900 ms after the click, and a 700 ms advance would have missed the stamp. The product timing should be decided separately.
- **Extra checks.** I used my own capture script (scratchpad/tools/seq.mjs) for the wrong-answer states and the Timed card change. Those captures are in the scratchpad, not in shots.

The decisions you need to make are listed under openQuestions for each screen.

review.systemNotes:
TOKENS. Every day screen's :root is byte-identical to game-classic.html. Both night screens share one identical night :root: the 17 reference tokens remapped, plus four additions that are commented in the file and reported here: --on-accent, --shadow-sm, --shadow-btn and --shadow-press. I recommend adding the three shadow tokens and a --scrim token to the day :root as well (the day values are the reference's own literals), because day screens still hard-code them. There are two leftover one-off alphas: home-a scrim rgba(ink,.32) and home-b's upward peek shadow (.5). No stray colours anywhere.

WHAT I STANDARDISED
- Screen title role: Overpass 800, 24px, line-height 1.1, letter-spacing -.015em, on the 16px margin, with an optional subtitle in Overpass Mono 400 12px ink. It was 28, 26 and 22px across home-a, home-b and mode-select.
- Filter chip: a 48px button with 40px raised paper drawn by ::before, active state ink paper with on-dark text, focus ring on the paper (home-a now matches home-b).
- List rows: deck code mono 600 22px; row title Overpass 600 16px; mono sub-lines 12px; section code mono 600 18px; trailing navigation is a muted 16px chevron icon. A '→' glyph only appears inside buttons and links that move forward (Next card, Start round, Choose a section, source link).
- Boarding pass legs: code always 34px (home-b was 40).
- Header control: a 48px raised round button with 16px icons at stroke 2.4. X means leave (game and result screens), ← means back (mode-select), and the sunk variant is used only on paper (the home-a sheet).
- Elevation: three recipes only: --shadow (boarding pass), small (round button, chip, deck cell), button (pills). home-c's deck cells moved onto the small recipe.
- Case: sentence case everywhere. Uppercase mono is reserved for the carrier band label (BOARDING PASS, DEPARTURES), as on the reference.
- Verbs: 'Choose' (Choose a deck, Choose a section, Choose how to play). I removed 'Pick', the unclear 'Choose route', and 'mode', which never appears in the UI. 'Class' is the in-UI word for mode because it is printed on the pass, and mode-select explains it.
- Placeholder: a destination not yet chosen is shown as three rule-coloured dashes over a muted two-line note (home-a sheet, home-b).
- Result screens: one layout (mono score block, sunk missed-cards slip with 'Why' disclosure and fade, 60px ink 'Play again', quiet 'Choose another route' with the route icon). The stamp is reserved for real verdicts: Correct, Not quite, New best.
- Data: section card counts follow home-a (CON 52, SEC 64, TEC 70, BIL 28 = 214); mode-select said 47.

LEFT DIFFERENT ON PURPOSE (each home is an alternative): deck progress is drawn three ways (home-a: dashed track with a plane dot; home-b: arc flight path; home-c: solid bar), and area headings two ways (home-a: mono 12 inside the boarding pass; home-c: sans 800 20 on the sky). Once a home is chosen, its version becomes the standard.

COMPONENT INVENTORY (screens that use it)
1. Sky backdrop: 4 bands plus 2 clouds (all).
2. Round button, raised (game-*, result-*, mode-select) and sunk (home-a sheet).
3. Flight path header: route SVG with waypoints (done circle with tick, wrong square with x, plane on accent, open future dots, end ring) plus a mono label row with progress left and tally right. Variants: count (game-classic, night), streak with best ring (game-streak), lives with hearts and mini path (game-lives), clock (game-timed), completed (result-classic, result-timed, result-classic-night).
4. Boarding pass: carrier band (accent, glyph, title, uppercase mono label); legs (34px code and name, with fly arrow); meta strip (3 fields, mono 10.5 label over mono 600 15 value); perforation with side notches; stub (mono row, barcode, hint); sunk slip. Used by game-*, mode-select, result-*, home-c (Last round), home-a (Departures), home-b (deck pass variant with a band per deck).
5. Statement (Overpass 600 25/32): game-*.
6. Answer slip: answer, stamp, explanation, source link (game-classic, game-streak, game-lives, night).
7. Stamp: 3px double border, rotated -6°, spring land (game answers, game-timed on the stub, result-timed New best).
8. Swipe hint row plus drag intent stamps (game-*).
9. Pill button, 60px: False/True pair, ink primary (Next card, Start round, Play again, Choose a section), compact 48px variant (home-c Continue), disabled-between-cards state (game-timed).
10. Quiet button, 48px with leading icon (results).
11. Filter chip (home-a, home-b).
12. Deck row (home-a; home-c as a horizontal mini pass with stub and expand toggle).
13. Section row with code, name, count or last score, and chevron (home-a sheet, home-c slip).
14. Deck progress indicator (3 variants, see above).
15. Bottom sheet with grab bar and scrim (home-a). Accordion slip (home-c). Wallet stack with peeking bands (home-b).
16. Option row with radio check, name, description and best (mode-select).
17. Score block: mono 48 value with 'of N' plus comparison text or stamp (results).
18. Missed-card item with 'Why' disclosure; scroll list with bottom fade (results).
19. Lives hearts, with full and lost-with-slash states (game-lives).
20. Destination placeholder dashes (home-a, home-b).

Screens: design/flow/screens. Fresh shots: design/flow/shots. game-classic.html was not modified. The old night result is backed up at <scratchpad>/result-classic-night.orig.html. Stale shots game-classic-night-litpass-alt-1/2.png from an earlier alternative were left untouched.
review.homeComparison:
HOME A, Departures board (one boarding pass containing area chips, a stats strip and an area-grouped list; tapping a deck opens a section sheet). Strengths: the densest and most scannable option, with every deck visible at the same weight. The chip row already scrolls sideways, so it takes 8 areas without layout change, and the list scrolls inside the boarding pass. The sheet copes with any number of sections and makes 'Whole deck' the clear first choice. Weaknesses: no shortcut back into the last round, so a returning player always taps deck, then section, then class. 'A list inside a boarding pass' stretches the metaphor (a departures board is not a boarding pass). The screen can feel like a utility table. At 8 areas and 40 decks: chips filter to about 5 decks per area, and the 'All' view is a long but orderly scroll at about 93px per row (about 3,700px). This scales best of the three.

HOME B, Wallet (decks as stacked boarding passes, with the front one showing seen progress, best streak and one action). Strengths: the most charming and most on-metaphor, it looks like a phone wallet of passes. Its front pass gives a rich, calm summary of one deck. Weaknesses: you only see one deck's detail at a time, comparing decks means bringing each one forward, and peeking bands show a name truncated after about 30 characters. It does not show platforms or sections until you commit, and it has no 'continue last round'. At 8 areas and 40 decks: every hidden deck costs a 52px band, so 'All' becomes about 2,000px of bands in a scroll region above a fixed front pass that already takes about 60% of the screen. Discovery collapses past about 6 decks unless the chips are always used. It works for 'my few decks' and fails as a catalogue.

HOME C, Itinerary (a 'Last round' boarding pass with a one-tap Continue, then area > platform > deck cells with inline section slips). Strengths: best for the most common case, a returning player, who gets one tap back into play. It is the only option that shows the real content model (area > platform > deck > section) and lets a player reach a section without leaving the screen. Its mini passes with a stub are the most crafted deck cells. Weaknesses: no area filter or jump, and the Last-round pass permanently takes about 290px, leaving about 400px for the catalogue. Opening a deck's slip pushes everything below it down. At 8 areas and 40 decks: about 90px per deck plus area and platform headers comes to about 4,500px of scrolling with no way to jump. Without changes it is the worst at scale.

RECOMMENDATION: C as the base, with two borrowings from A. First, A's area chips, placed under the Last-round pass and pinned when the pass scrolls away (the pass should scroll with the list, not stay fixed). Second, A's sheet as the fallback when a deck has more than about 6 sections. This keeps C's one-tap continue and true hierarchy and gets A's scaling. B's wallet front pass is the nicest single-deck summary and could become the header of the section sheet, but B should not be the home.
